header: These are pure post-ranking adjustments for the omnibar's circular search (semantic mode, Latin non-quoted queries only). I keep them free of DB, model and state: the same function is exercised offline against recorded battery results. Each rule is a statement a human reader would agree with:

1. YEAR A year in the question counts. A result whose own title states a different year is demoted; one that states the asked year is lifted. With no year in the question, the NEWEST holiday policy / holiday list wins, and older yearly copies of the same policy collapse.
2. AUDIENCE Contractor-worker circulars do not answer a question that never mentions contractors; regular-employee holiday documents do not answer a question about contractor workers.
3. HOLIDAYS For a holiday-topic question the holiday notes / holiday lists are the answer and must rank among the best.
4. CUTOFF When the best result is strong, results far below it are noise.
I return quoted and Indic-script queries untouched.

members.name: fromHeadlineEmbedding
doc: True for holiday-list circulars found only by headline embedding; they have no body text

members.name: margin
doc: I drop results more than this many points below the best (when best >= 85); default 12

members.name: maxHolidayLists
doc: The most headline-embedding holiday lists I keep when the question names no year

symbols.name: CONTRACT_QUERY_RE
doc: This is what a QUESTION says when it is about contractor workers: the headline word, but also the short forms people type ("CW", "labour", "workers"). I use it for the question only; headlines are tested with CONTRACT_RE.

symbols.name: yearsIn
doc: Returns every year a text states, including ranges: "2024-25" -> 2024, 2025; "01.01.2025" -> 2025.

symbols.name: collapseYearlyPolicyCopies
symbols.sig: export function collapseYearlyPolicyCopies<T extends RankItem>(q: string, items: T[]): T[]
doc: With no year in the question, I collapse yearly copies of the same holiday policy ("Compensatory Off (2020 holiday policy)" ... "(2026 holiday policy)") to the newest one, because the question is about the policy as it stands now. With a year in the question I return the list unchanged: the year rule ranks them instead.
